_README: SETTLED validator findings, with their evidence. Read by src/validate/fundamentals/
check_register.py; written only by a human reviewing an agent's proposal.
`fundamentals_check` (the TABLE) is append-only and grows every night. This file is what
makes the QUEUE shrink: a finding investigated once and settled here is subtracted from
every later run by its `finding_id`, so nothing is ever re-investigated.
WHY A GIT-TRACKED JSON AND NOT A `state` COLUMN. Two reasons, both learned: a mutable
column is lost on any table rebuild, and this project rebuilds these tables by design
(`fundamentals --rebuild`); and 'why was this accepted?' would then live in free text
outside version control. The evidence for an acceptance is the most valuable artifact the
loop produces -- it belongs where a diff can be reviewed.
THIS IS NOT A SUPPRESSION LIST. Every rule below exists to keep it from becoming one:
* `accepted` needs FILING-LEVEL evidence -- what was read, and where. A reason code is
the resolver's verdict, never evidence, and `not_disclosed` is a statement about our
concept MAP rather than about the filing.
* `fixed` needs BOTH a `commit` and a named `regression_test`. Precedent: four defects
were CREATED BY the 3c.1-3c.5 fixes and were visible only on a full re-sweep. A fix
with no test is a defect waiting to come back.
* `fixed` also carries `regression_swept`, false until a batched FULL-ROSTER sweep has
seen it. A per-finding close is scoped to the affected tickers and is provisional.
* `wontfix` needs a QUANTIFIED cost in `evidence` -- a number, not an adjective. NEE's
$5.2bn capex understatement is a defensible wontfix only because the number is here.
* `fix_kind: config_proposed` DOES NOT CLOSE A FINDING. `configs/` is the one artifact
where a wrong entry is invisible forever, so an agent proposes the diff and the
finding stays OPEN until a human approves it. The withdrawn 'UNH has no premiums'
edit was one approval away from being written.
* STALE ENTRIES ARE REPORTED every run -- a settled finding whose check no longer fires
-- so the register decays visibly instead of accumulating suppressions for defects
that were fixed somewhere else years ago.
`finding_id` is a deterministic hash of (check, ticker, field, period_key) and NOT of the
run date, the severity or the observed value. A threshold retune must not resurrect a
settled finding, and a re-measured value must not orphan one.
HAND-FORMATTED, like every other fundamentals config. A json.dumps round-trip reformats
the whole file and turns a one-entry change into a whole-file diff, which destroys the
reviewability this register exists for. `check_register.render_entry` emits one entry in
this style; splice it in.
EMPTY ON PURPOSE. Nothing has been settled yet: 5b-core.1 ships the mechanism, and the
first entries are written by the agent loop against real findings. An entry invented
before a finding exists would be a guess about a measurement -- which is exactly how the
withdrawn UNH edit nearly happened.

_schema.finding_id: 16 hex chars; the cross-run identity. See finding.py::finding_id.
_schema.check: the CHECK_REGISTRY name that produced it
_schema.ticker: the filer, or '' for a universe-level finding
_schema.field: the catalogue field, or '' for a ticker-level check
_schema.period_key: as_of | period_end | 'start..end' | '' -- polymorphic by the check's grain
_schema.fix_kind: code | config_proposed | null. config_proposed does NOT close the finding.
_schema.regression_test: required when outcome == fixed: the test that pins the case forever
_schema.regression_swept: false until a batched full-roster sweep has confirmed the fix
_schema.evidence: prose. For accepted: what was read in which accession. For wontfix: a NUMBER.
